🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexicana Is Back: State Airline Plans 20 Planes by 2027</u>

Mexicana de Aviación, the airline the neoliberal era let die and the 4T brought back as a state carrier, presented its growth plan at the mañanera: 12 aircraft by the end of 2026, 20 by 2027, break-even and profit from 2030. Seat capacity up 83% since June, passengers up 31% this year, more than 1.276 million flown since launch and over 840 direct jobs. "This seat capacity has allowed us to serve the different markets and destinations Mexicana flies to," said director Leobardo Ávila Bojórquez. AIFA–Zacatecas launches November 17.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>State Prisons Failing: 258 of 261 Can't Even Separate Inmates</u>

Mexico's human rights commission (CNDH) released its 2025 National Prison Supervision Diagnostic: improper classification of inmates in 258 of the 261 state prisons inspected, 98.9%. Overcrowding in 124 of them, failing grades as low as 4.37 out of 10, and 28 state systems scoring worse than in 2024 while only four improved. The CNDH is calling for authorities to "recover governability" of the prisons. Today a riot in a Sinaloa prison left nine inmates and a minor dead.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum Takes the Health System Review on the Road: 23 States, Hospital by Hospital</u>

Starting today in Hidalgo and this weekend in Estado de México, the President will spend until December touring every state where IMSS-Bienestar runs free public healthcare, with Health Secretary David Kershenobich and IMSS-Bienestar chief Alejandro Svarch. "I will meet with the directors of every hospital and the coordinators, to listen to them, to see what the problems are and what is missing." Facilities, staffing, digital clinical records: a universal health system gets built from the ground floor, not from a desk.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico Cut Irregular Border Crossings 98%. Washington Still Talks About "Invasion"</u>

Sheinbaum laid out the numbers at Palacio Nacional in front of Ambassador Ronald Johnson and AmCham: irregular crossings into the US from Mexico's northern border down 98%, fentanyl seizures in the US down 75%, and roughly 94 cartel bosses handed over to US justice. Mexico's approach: give migrants jobs at home or help them get back to where they came from, before they ever reach the wall. Cooperation, not subordination, and the results are on the table.

🇲🇽📊 <u>Only 4 in 10 Mexican Companies With Income Paid Income Tax</u>

Of the roughly 500,000 companies that reported positive income for 2025, only 40% paid income tax, and just 10% paid an effective rate above 2.5%, against a legal rate of 30%, Deputy Finance Secretary Carlos Lerma told the Chamber of Deputies' Finance Committee (El Economista). The 2027 budget package caps deductions at 96.66% of income and loss carryforwards at 50% of the year's profit for firms billing over 50 million pesos. Individuals, RESICO taxpayers and companies under five years old are exempt. "Collecting with justice makes it possible to sustain medical care, education and support for those who need it most," Lerma said.

🇲🇽✈️ <u>AIFA Passes 22.6 Million Passengers</u>

Since opening on March 21, 2022, the Felipe Ángeles International Airport has moved more than 22.6 million passengers. It went from 4 airlines to 7, from 6 domestic destinations to 40, and from 1 international route to 7, and it has handled over 1.358 million tons of cargo. The airport the opposition swore nobody would use broke even in the first quarter of 2024, employs 18,000 people directly and now ranks sixth in Mexico by passenger traffic.

🇲🇽🗳️ <u>Sheinbaum: Claim That Washington Picked Morena's Candidates Is "Absurd"</u>

PT national leader Alberto Anaya claimed US pressure shaped Morena's choice of state coordinators for 2027, when 17 governorships and the entire Chamber of Deputies are on the ballot. Sheinbaum's answer at Thursday's mañanera: "It's absurd, really, what he's saying has no basis at all." Morena has picked its coordinators by poll since its founding, she said, and sometimes the person a party wanted doesn't come out on top, "and they make these interpretations that have no basis."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Crucifix, Skull and Dagger: The Secret Anti-Communist Lodge Inside UNAM</u>

Mexican intelligence files from the DFS and DGIPS held in the Archivo General de la Nación, plus a declassified CIA document, reconstruct for the first time how the MURO worked inside UNAM in the 1960s: recruits from elite Catholic schools, a secret oath sworn before a crucifix, a skull and a dagger, shock brigades that broke up leftist meetings with tear gas, and members planted at the head of student societies without revealing who they answered to. Business sectors close to alemanismo helped fund its propaganda. The CIA's own file from August 5, 1965 described the group as "fascist and antisemitic."

🇲🇽🏭 <u>800 Miners Strike at Canadian-Owned First Majestic Mine in Durango</u>

At noon on October 8, Sections 21 and 22 of Mexico's National Mining Union raised red-and-black strike flags over the Tayoltita underground gold and silver mine in San Dimas, Durango. The charges against Canada's First Majestic: violations of the collective contract and of union freedom, deteriorated machinery kept running on provisional repairs, accidents that have cost workers' lives, and a profit-based bonus for 2025 that was owed in 2026 and never paid.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Sheinbaum Hosts 30+ US and Mexican Business Leaders at the National Palace</u>

US Ambassador Ronald Johnson and the American Chamber of Commerce sat down with President Sheinbaum for an hour and a half on Thursday. On the table: confidence in Mexico as a destination for US investment and closing out the T-MEC review. CCE president José Medina Mora called it a high-level meeting and said the American executives left very happy that the President listened to their plans to expand. The numbers behind the mood: foreign direct investment hit $35 billion in the first half of 2026, 14% above 2024, and this year's growth forecast has been revised from 0.8% to 1.5%.
